tasks.spec:
Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Edit files there directly. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production change with no tests, fewer than 3 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these):
  server/pipeline/av_sync.py
  tests/test_av_sync.py

THE PROBLEM, observed across repeated real runs. The stems builder in server/pipeline/av_sync.py re-renders the four per-speaker stem files (processed/stems/*.flac, *.mp4) on every pipeline run. The stem CONTENT is deterministic and content-pinned (timeline.json records sha256 over the stems; verify_stem_content_pin), so consecutive runs write byte-identical files — but with fresh mtimes. Downstream artifacts built from stems in an earlier run (e.g. the Whisper transcript, which is expensive and content-cached) then look OLDER than their inputs, and the certification freshness gate (an mtime DAG check) reports them stale even though nothing changed. Every run re-poisons the mtime DAG and would force pointless re-transcription to stay certified.

THE FIX: make stem writes idempotent on content. In the code path that produces each stem file, render to a temporary file in the same directory, then compare content against an existing stem at the destination (hash comparison, e.g. sha256 of both files — cheap relative to the render; reuse an existing hashing helper if the module has one). If the destination exists AND content is identical: keep the EXISTING file untouched (preserve its mtime; remove the temp). If different or absent: atomically replace (os.replace). The content pin, downstream behavior, and stem bytes must be unchanged in every case — this only stops gratuitous mtime churn. Apply it to every stem artifact the builder writes (audio and video stems). Log one line per stem: reused-identical vs replaced.

TESTS (tests/test_av_sync.py additions, mock the actual rendering with tiny real temp files, at least 3 new tests): (1) writing the same content twice leaves the destination inode/mtime untouched (capture os.stat before/after; assert equal mtime_ns); (2) NEGATIVE: writing different content DOES replace the file and the new content is what remains; (3) a missing destination is created; (4) the temp file never survives in the stems dir in any branch (assert directory listing contains only expected names).
tasks.verified: byte-identical stem re-renders no longer touch mtimes, so the freshness DAG stays truthful across runs
